The contractual remedies for buying defective goods (those of unsatisfactory quality) still remain under the Sale and Supply of Goods Act 1994. Which of the following statements best describes what 'goods'
ask: Which of the following statements best describes what 'goods' are for the purposes of the CPA?

options.en: For the purposes of the CA goods are defined as substances; crops; things comprised in land by virtue of being attached to it; ships; aircraft; vehicles; and the supply of gas, water or electricity

For the purposes of the CPA goods are defined as substances; crops; things comprised in land by virtue of being attached to it; ships; aircraft; vehicles; the supply of gas, water or electricity; and professional services

For the purposes of the CA goods are defined as substances; crops; things comprised in land by virtue of being attached to it; ships; aircraft; vehicles; the supply of gas, water or electricity; and buildings

For the purposes of the CPA goods are defined as substances; crops; things comprised in land by virtue of being attached to it; ships; aircraft; vehicles; the supply of gas, water or electricity; professional services; and buildings

For the purposes of the CPA goods are defined as substances; crops; things comprised in land by virtue of being attached to it; ships; aircraft; vehicles; the supply of gas, water or electricity; professional services; buildings; and printed material

explanation.en: the purposes of the CPA goods are defined as substances; crops; things comprised in land by virtue of being attached to it; ships; aircraft; vehicles; and the supply of gas, water or electricity. Statute; rule; constitution: s. 45(1) Consumer Protection Act 1987.

stem: Your client's investment manager was bribed to invest your client's funds into a fraudulent share scheme involving a time share company. Whilst the people who bribed your client's investment manager are not servants or agents of the time share company, the managing director of the time share company knew of them and their tactics and it was the managing director who signed - on the company's behalf - the agreement between your client's investment manager and the company. Your client wants to know his recovery options.
ask: Against whom can your client recover under the doctrine of recipient liability?

options.en: Your client can recover against the time share company
Your client can recover against the investment manager
Your client can recover against those who bribed the investment manager
Your client can recover against any of the time share company, investment manager or those who bribed the investment manager
Your client has no recovery options

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The best answer is A. Your client can recover against the time share company. Under the doctrine of recipient liability, a disposal is required of the claimant's assets in breach of fiduciary duty, the receipt of those assets by the defendant and constructive knowledge on the part of the defendant that the assets are attributable to the breach of the fiduciary duty - per El Ajoy v Dollar Land Holdings plc [1993] 3 All ER 717. The recipient's state of knowledge must be such as to make it unconscionable for him to retain the benefit of the receipt - BCCI v Akindele [2000] 3 WLR 1423. In this case, the recipient of the funds is the time share company. Since the managing director committed the investment manager likely knew about), the managing director would likely be found to be the 'directing mind and will of the company, with the requisite knowledge and conduct to render the company liable under the doctrine of knowing receipt.

stem: A director of a company personally owns 50 acres of land. He wishes to sell some of this land to the company at the market value of £200,000. He believes he can do so without limitation.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the situation?

options.en: There are no limitations to the director selling the land to the company
Transactions cannot be made between a company and a director
The transaction must be approved by an ordinary resolution at a general meeting or a written resolution
A director can only buy assets from the company, they cannot sell assets to the company
The transaction must be approved by a written resolution only

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is C. When there is a transaction of a non-cash asset over £100,000 (or 10% of the company's net value) between a director and their company, it must be approved by an ordinary resolution at a general meeting or a written resolution.

stem: Carl, 52, Mark, 48 and John, 44, are friends. In each of their wills they leave all their assets to each other. For example, Carl's assets will go to Mark and John upon his death. If either Mark or John is deceased, then the surviving beneficiary inherits all of the estate. Similarly, if Mark dies his estate will go to Carl and John or whichever of them is the surviving beneficiary. When Carl and Mark are both killed in a boating accident, John is the sole beneficiary of each estate. He believes that as he is inheriting on one occasion (rather than two separate occasions) he will only pay Inheritance Tax (IHT) on one property.
ask: Which of the following best describes the current legal position?

options.en: John will only pay IHT once
The two estates will be combined and John will pay IHT once on the total of both estates
Neither estate will be liable for IHT, regardless of their respective values
If the value of each estate exceeds the threshold then John will pay IHT on both estates
John cannot inherit both estates

explanation.topic: Wills and the Administration of Estates
explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is D. Each estate is separate and will be assessed individually. Therefore, if the estates exceed the threshold for IHT John will pay the tax on each estate separately.

stem: A passenger on a bus saw another bus hurtling towards it. In order to avoid being injured, he opened the emergency door and was about to jump, but grabbed a child and jumped with the child in his arms. The child was injured on the impact landing.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the standard of care required in the case of an emergency?

options.en: In the case of an emergency where a defendant makes a wrong but reasonable • decision in the heat of the moment, he should not be liable, provided he acts as an ordinary skilled person exercising and professing to have that particular skill

In the case of an emergency where a defendant makes a wrong but reasonable decision in the heat of the moment, he should not be liable, provided he acts to the standard of the reasonably competent rescuer

In the case of an emergency where a defendant makes a wrong but reasonable • decision in the heat of the moment, he should not be liable, provided he acts as a reasonable and prudent person would have done

In the case of an emergency where a defendant makes a wrong but reasonable decision in the heat of the moment, he should not be liable, provided he does not act with reckless disregard of his or others' safety

In the case of an emergency where a defendant makes a wrong but reasonable decision in the heat of the moment, it is the same as in any other situation, since no wrong is done to a person who consents to it

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is correct. Where the claimant is placed in a position of imminent danger by the negligence of the defendant, the courts are more sympathetic towards the defendant who makes a wrongful decision in the heat of the moment, provided he acts as a reasonable and prudent man would have done.

stem: A man lived on the 12th floor of a high-rise block of flats and liked to watch soap operas all day, because he was long-term unemployed. One day, his television stopped working. Rather than carry it down to be disposed of, without thinking about the consequences, he threw it over the balcony, where it landed on an 11 year- old girl below, killing her instantly.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the man's criminal liability, if any?

options.en: The man's likely criminal liability is for voluntary manslaughter
The man's likely criminal liability is for involuntary manslaughter
The man's likely criminal liability is for constructive manslaughter
The man's likely criminal liability is for gross negligence manslaughter
The man would not be criminally liable because an unlawful act must constitute a crime; negligence is insufficient

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is correct. B isn't wrong, but C is the best answer. The mens rea for constructive manslaughter is different from that of murder. Essentially, it is the mens rea for the unlawful act that counts. Moreover, it is not necessary for the prosecution to show that the defendant needed to realise that there was a risk that he would cause harm with his actions, merely that he intended to undertake the action. Lead case: DPP v Newbury and Jones [1976].

stem: A woman executes a will in which, after making certain specific bequests, she leaves "the remainder of my estate to my daughter, to be held on trust until she attains the age of 30.
ask: " Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The woman has created a valid trust
The trust has failed for lack of certainty of intention and objects
The trust has failed for lack of certainty of subject matter
The trust has failed for lack of certainty of subject matter and objects
The trust has failed for lack of certainty of subject matter and intention

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is A. The trust has certainty of intention due to the woman's use of the word "trust", which is appropriate technical language that conveys a definite intention to form a trust. The beneficiary (the daughter) is clearly identified in the trust instrument and therefore certainty of objects exists. Although no specific property is identified by the instrument, the term "the remainder of my estate" is a necessarily certain term denoting the entirety of the woman's estate after the specific bequests have been made.

stem: A Non-governmental Organisation (NGO) has demanded that the British government call off the threatened eviction of travellers from an illegal traveller's site near Birmingham. Local residents opposed to the site successfully applied to the High Court, and then successfully contested an appeal by the travellers, who alleged that the eviction is in breach of their rights under the European Convention on Human Rights (the Convention). A spokesperson for the NGO wishes to know the scope of the European Court of Human Rights' (ECtHR) jurisdiction to hear the travellers' allegations against the British government.
ask: Which option best advises the NGO's spokesperson?

options.en: The ECtHR can commence a case of its own motion
The ECtHR can commence a case of its own motion only after an applicant has exhausted all domestic remedies
The ECtHR cannot commence a case of its own motion
The ECtHR cannot commence a case of its own motion unless the applicant's complaint is founded on a right mentioned in the Convention or its Protocols

The ECtHR cannot commence a case of its own motion unless the applicant has exhausted all domestic remedies and the applicant's complaint is founded on a right mentioned in the Convention or its Protocols

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is the best option. The ECtHR jurisdiction is invoked when it receives an application from an individual party alleging that a contracting State has violated its rights, or from a contracting State that alleges a violation by another contracting State. If the ECtHR considers that a case is admissible, it may then seek further details and receive further submissions from the parties. The ECtHR cannot, however, commence a case of its own motion. Therefore its jurisdiction only allows it to hear complaints regarding breaches of the Convention after individual or inter-State applications are initiated.

stem: A woman owns 76% of the issued share capital of a private limited company. Her daughter owns the remaining 24%. A solicitor and an accountant are employees of a business services firm and act as the company's directors, a service that they carry out in their professional capacities. It becomes clear that insolvent liquidation of the company is inevitable. However, the woman insists that they continue to trade, failing which she will terminate their appointment as directors. The solicitor and accountant's boss insists that they continue to trade the company as he does not want to lose the work.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: There is no wrongful trading
There has been wrongful trading. As the solicitor and accountant are the company's directors, they are solely personally responsible for this
There has been wrongful trading. As the solicitor and accountant are the company's directors, they are solely personally responsible for this unless otherwise provided for by an ordinary resolution
There has been wrongful trading. The solicitor and accountant would be personally liable for this as the company's directors and the woman would be personally liable as a shadow director
There has been wrongful trading. The solicitor and accountant would be liable for this as the company's directors and the woman and her daughter would be liable as its members

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is D. Wrongful trading has taken place as the directors have continued to trade the company when it is clear that the company will go into liquidation. The solicitor and accountant would be personally liable to contribute to the liquidation as they are directors. Due to her having a controlling share in the company, the woman would also be personally liable to contribute as a shadow director. It is unlikely that the daughter would be regarded as a shadow director, as she has no controlling share in the company, and accordingly she would escape liability. une hung. Would be

stem: Builders used a pile-driver drill during the night on a building site near the claimant's hotel. The hotel owner claims this action has caused him to lose business.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the three elements required to establish nuisance?

options.en: There are three elements that characterise nuisance: (1) the claimant must have • a substantial link with the property affected; (2) damage to the claimant; and (3) unreasonable interference
There are three elements that characterise nuisance: (1) indirect interference with the enjoyment of land; (2) damage to the claimant; and (3) the defendant was at fault

There are three elements that characterise nuisance: (1) indirect interference with the enjoyment of land; (2) the defendant failed to exercise reasonable care and skill; and (3) unreasonable interference
There are three elements that characterise nuisance: (1) indirect interference with the enjoyment of land; (2) damage to the claimant; and (3) unreasonable interference

There are three elements that characterise nuisance: (1) indirect interference with the enjoyment of land; (2) damage to the claimant; and (3) a sufficient relationship of proximity between the claimant and the defendant

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. D is correct. The three elements that characterise nuisance are: (1) indirect interference with the enjoyment of land; (2) damage to the claimant; and (3) unreasonable interference.

stem: In a judgement delivered by Lord Justice Smith, it is noted in his reasoning that another division of the court had reached a decision by failing to take into account all the relevant and vital statutes or case authorities. Due to this oversight, Smith L noted, this had a major effect on the decision. He expressed the view that the decision in question was so manifestly wrong that the court was not bound by it.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the rule applied in this case?

options.en: Amicus curiae means that a court failed to take into account all the relevant and vital statutes or case authorities and that this had a major effect on the decision
Ratio decidendi means that a court failed to take into account all the relevant and vital statutes or case authorities and that this had a major effect on the decision
Ejusdem Generis means that a court failed to take into account all the relevant • and vital statutes or case authorities and that this had a major effect on the decision
The Golden Rule means that a court failed to take into account all the relevant and vital statutes or case authorities and that this had a major effect on the decision
Per incuriam means that a court failed to take into account all the relevant and vital statutes or case authorities and that this had a major effect on the decision

explanation.en: E is correct. Per incuriam does not signify mere carelessness on the part of the court, or the fact that the case or judgment was badly reasoned. It is confined to the narrow grounds of failure to consider binding authority or statute.

stem: In 2011 your client purchased a second property for £150,000 and spent £50,000 on improving the property. He sold it in 2015 for £450,000, making a capital gain of £300,000. Your client wants to know if he can reduce his capital gain by £50,000 for the money spent on improving the property.
ask: Which of the following best describe the current legal position?

The cost of improvements is considered routine maintenance and so cannot be deducted
The cost of improvements can be deducted from the capital gain and will reduce your client's capital gain to £250,000
Half the cost of improvements can be deducted from the capital gain and will reduce your client's capital gain to £125,000
The cost of improvements can only be deducted if they are objectively seen as • being the cause of the capital gain and that the capital gain hasn't arisen via other means

stem: The defendant claims that he was suffering from a mental illness at the time of entering in to contractual relations with the claimant and that he was incapable of understanding what he was doing. The defendant asserts that the claimant was aware of his mental incapacity and seeks to avoid the contract.
ask: Which option best the legal position?

options.en: The defendant must prove that he did not understand the nature of the contract; and the claimant was aware of his impairment
The defendant must prove that the terms of the contract, taken as a whole, were not for his benefit; and the other party was aware of his impairment
The claimant must prove that he was unaware of the defendant's impairment
The claimant must prove that the defendant understood the nature of the contract and that he (the claimant) was not aware of his impairment
The defendant must prove that the terms of the contract, taken as a whole, were not for his benefit

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. A is the best option. The defendant must prove that he did not understand the nature of the contract; and the claimant was aware of his impairment. Under common law, a contract made by a person who, by reason of mental abnormality, is incapable of understanding what he is doing is valid unless he can prove: (a) he did not understand the nature of the contract, and (b) the other party was aware of his impairment. Accordingly, where a defendant argued that he was insane at the time of making a promissory note and that the claimant knew this, the court held that the defendant had to convince the court on both issues; not just that he was insane at the time.

stem: In breach of its statutory duty, a supermarket sold food that had been contaminated. Apparently someone working in the food's primary production added a substance to it in its preparation which had not been approved by the relevant authorities. A retailer has been charged with rendering the food injurious to health.
ask: Which option best states the principal defence to a charge under a statutory offence?

options.en: There is no defence relevant to such regulatory offences because these are virtually always strict liability offences, meaning that the defendant's mind is irrelevant once the threshold of the offence has been proven
The principal defence relevant to regulatory offences and common across statutes is that of contributory negligence
The principal defence relevant to regulatory offences and common across statutes is that of contributory negligence volenti non fit injuria "no wrong is done to one who consents"
The principal defence relevant to regulatory offences and common across statutes is that of consent
The principal defence relevant to regulatory offences and common across statutes is that of due diligence

explanation.en: E is the best option. The principal defence relevant to regulatory offences and common across statutes is that of due diligence. Negligence is rarely sufficient to qualify as a state of mind amounting to a criminal offence. Absence of negligence, however, can be put forward as a defence to some statutory offences. For example, the foremost defence relevant to regulatory offences and common across statutes is that of due diligence. Due diligence can be said to be the converse of negligence. It is integral to the organisation of a defence of due diligence, therefore, that the facts of the offence must be made out before the question of due diligence arises. Section 21 of the Food Safety Act 1990 provides a homely example of the type of source, it is a defence if the seller can show that he acted with due diligence in order to prevent the commission of an offence and was, therefore, not negligent. In the context of the fact pattern, it likely that the retailer could have checked by proper due diligence whether the substance had been approved by the authorities before using it.

stem: A woman is diagnosed with a terminal illness and wishes to ensure that her daughter is properly provided for after she dies. The daughter is 17 but has never learned how to handle money very well. The woman wishes to ensure that the daughter is not able to gain access to the woman's estate until she is mature enough to handle it properly and wishes to leave the trustees with enough discretion to react to any change in the daughter's circumstances.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the type of trust that the woman should create?

options.en: The woman should create a dynasty trust
The woman should create a spendthrift trust
The woman should create an incentive trust
The woman should create a purpose trust

stem: You are instructed to act for a firm of solicitors incorporated as a limited liability partnership (LLP). The partnership is rebranding itself and wishes to change its name. It has a very detailed partnership agreement in place, but the provision in respect of the change of name only states: "The name of the partnership may be changed, subject to notice of the change being communicated to all parties within 24 hours of the decision being approved." Other provisions of the agreement vary in the required amount of members required to pass a decision.
ask: Which of the following best explains how the name of the LLP can be changed?

options.en: The clause in the partnership agreement is fully effective and, in the absence of • a specific majority of members required to change the LLP's name, a simple majority is all that is needed
The clause in the partnership agreement is fully effective and, in the absence of a specific majority of members required to change the LLP's name, a majority of 75% is needed
The clause in the partnership agreement is fully effective and, in the absence of • a specific majority of members required to change the LLP's name, a majority of 100% is needed

The clause in the partnership agreement is effective only in that it conditionally permits the name to be changed; in the absence of a specific majority of members required to change the LLP's name, the default provisions apply and a majority of 100% is needed

Since the changing of an LLP's name is not contained in any legislation, and the clause in the partnership does not state the majority of members required to effect such a change, it is invalidly drafted and the LLP has no statutory power to change its name

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is D. The clause in the partnership agreement is effective only in that it conditionally permits the name to be changed; in the absence of a specific majority of members required to change the LLP's name, the default provisions apply and a majority of 100% is needed. Under Section 5(1) of the Limited Liability Partnership Regulations 2001 (the Regulations), the mutual rights and duties of an LLP and its members are governed by an agreement between the members. There are no statutory provisions governing whether and how an LLP can change its name. The LLP is therefore free to change its name, subject to the of the partnership agreement, which in this case place a conditional requirement that notice be communicated on the change of name. In the absence of an express provision in the partnership agreement or in general law, the default provisions contained in Section 7 of the Regulations apply. Since there is no provision in respect of the majority of members required to change the LLP's name, and the partnership agreement contains varying majority requirements for different decisions, the default provisions apply. stem: A woman and man own 123 The Street together as joint tenants. The man executes a declaration of trust in favour of his friend.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The woman and man hold the property on trust for themselves as tenants in common in equal shares
The woman and man hold the property on trust for the woman and the man's friend as tenants in common in equal shares
The woman and man hold the property on trust for the woman and the man's friend as joint tenants
The woman and man hold the property on trust for themselves as joint tenants
The woman and the man's friend hold the property on trust for themselves as joint tenants

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is B. The man has transferred his equitable interest in the property to his friend, but he retains legal title to the property, which he holds as a trustee. As the woman and the friend would not have unity of title, they would hold the equitable interest as tenants in common.

stem: A fur coat is offered to a woman in a pub at a low price by a man, who is known as a criminal type. The woman suspects the fur coat might be stolen, but the man assures her that it is not. In fact, it had been stolen, and the woman has subsequently been arrested for handling stolen goods.
ask: Which of the following states the woman's criminal liability, if any, for handling stolen?

options.en: The woman is criminally liable for handling stolen goods if she suspected that the goods were stolen
The woman is criminally liable for handling stolen goods if she suspected or believed that the goods were stolen
The woman is criminally liable for handling stolen goods if she knew or suspected that the goods were stolen
The woman is criminally liable for handling stolen goods if she supposed or suspected that the goods were stolen
The woman is criminally liable for handling stolen goods if she knew or believed that the goods were stolen

explanation.en: E is correct. The mens rea for handling stolen goods requires the defendant to know or believe that the goods are stolen. Statute; Rule; Constitution: Theft Act s22.

stem: In the study of the law of tort, the centre stage is occupied by the tort of negligence. This tort imposes liability for a failure to take proper care to avoid inflicting foreseeable injury, e.g.
ask: an occupier of premises who knows that the premises are in a dangerous condition, yet fails to make them safe and injury is caused to a visitor as a Which of the following statements best defines which three elements a claimant must prove to succeed in an action for negligence?

options.en: The three elements a claimant must prove to succeed in an action for negligence are: (1) carelessness; (2) a breach of that duty; and (3) damage
The three elements a claimant must prove to succeed in an action for negligence are: (1) a duty of care; (2) a breach of that duty; and (3) damage
The three elements a claimant must prove to succeed in an action for negligence are: (1) negligence; (2) a breach of the duty of care; and (3) damage
The three elements a claimant must prove to succeed in an action for negligence are: (1) a foreseeability of harm; (2) a breach of the duty of care; and (3) damage
The three elements a claimant must prove to succeed in an action for negligence are: (1) causation; (2) a breach of the duty of care; and (3) damage

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. B is correct. The three elements a claimant must prove to succeed in an action for negligence are: (1) a duty of care; (2) a breach of that duty; and (3) damage. Lead case: Blyth v Birmingham Waterworks Co (1856).

stem: Your client brought her favourite cocktail dress for dry cleaning. She was asked by the assistant to sign a receipt containing a widely worded exemption clause and was innocently but wrongly told that the clause meant that the dry cleaning company would not accept liability for damage to the beads and sequins which adorned the dress. When it was returned the dress had a stain on it, but the dry cleaning company is relying on the exclusion clause which really excluded liability for all damage to the dress whatsoever.
ask: Which of the following statements best advises whether the dry cleaning company can rely on the exclusion clause?

options.en: The dry cleaning company cannot rely on the exclusion clause, because a fraudulent misrepresentation renders the exclusion clause ineffective
The dry cleaning company can rely on the exclusion clause, because even if there had been a misrepresentation, it was a wholly innocent misrepresentation
The dry cleaning company can rely on the exclusion clause, because your client voluntarily signed the document; there was a signed contract in place
The dry cleaning company cannot rely on the exclusion clause, because a • misrepresentation, even if wholly innocent, outweighs the fact that your client had signed the document
The dry cleaning company can rely on the exclusion clause, because in the absence of fraud an exclusion clause is always effective

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. D is correct. Because the extent of the exclusion was misrepresented, the dry cleaning company would effectively be estopped from relying upon it.

stem: A girl, aged 2, is the beneficiary of a trust of shares created by her aunt's will, which was executed on 6 April 2010. The girl's parents are themselves very wealthy and they meet all of the costs of the girl's maintenance. The trust generates a significant annual income and is not due to vest in the girl until she is 25. The trustees approach you for advice as to what they should do with the income.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The trustees must pay the income generated by the trust to the girl
The trustees may accumulate the income produced by the trust but for no longer than 21 years
The trustees may accumulate the income produced by the trust but for no longer than 25 years
The trustees must accumulate the income produced by the trust for the remainder of the trust period
The trustees may accumulate the income produced by the trust for the remainder of the trust period

explanation.en: The correct answer is E. The Perpetuities and Accumulations Act 2009 would apply to the trust because it was executed on the commencement date for the Act. The Act provides that income can be accumulated within the trust for the whole of the trust period (this was previously limited to 21 years). However there is no requirement to do so - the trustees have a statutory power of maintenance and can use that to distribute accumulated income if they wish to do so.

stem: The European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) has become a tool for European citizens to benefit from an effective guarantee for respect of Human Rights. However, 96 per cent of applications are summarily rejected by the ECtHR. One third of all applications are dismissed on administrative grounds.
ask: Which of the following best states how the ECtHR ascertains the admissibility of the remainder of applications?

options.en: The remainder of applications is generally dismissed by a two-judge filtering committee
The remainder of applications is generally dismissed by a three-judge filtering committee
The remainder of applications is generally dismissed by a five judge filtering committee
The remainder of applications is generally dismissed by a seven-judge filtering committee
The remainder of applications is generally dismissed by a nine-judge filtering committee

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. B is correct. Committees of three judges ascertain the admissibility of the applications.

stem: A woman is the freehold owner of 123 The Street. She grants a lease by parol to a man for 12 months at a market rent. The arrangement is not recorded in writing. Six months into the tenancy, the woman changes her mind and wishes to recover possession. She arranges for the gas and electricity supply to be disconnected, hoping that this will cause the man to become fed up and leave the property.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The woman is in breach of an implied covenant for quiet enjoyment
The woman is in breach of an express covenant for quiet enjoyment
The woman is in breach of an implied covenant not to derogate from grant
The woman is in breach of an express covenant not to derogate from grant
As no written agreement was entered into, the woman has not given the man any covenants that can be breached

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is A. Although no written agreement has been entered into, the law still implies covenants on the part of the landlord into the agreement which must be observed. This includes the covenant for quiet enjoyment, that is to say a covenant that the landlord will not physically interfere with the tenant's use of the land.

stem: An anti-fast food campaigner had been sued for libel by a fast-food chain over an internet blog he posted. After a highly complex trial lasting over a year, the fast food chain was partially successful and the campaigner was ordered to pay damages of £50,000 for not proving on the balance of probabilities that his assertions were true. The campaigner was denied legal aid.
ask: Which statement best describes how, if at all, the court's decision engages the European Convention on Human Rights (the Convention)?

options.en: It shows that some of the fast-food chain's functions must have been of a hybrid, or public/private nature, for the complaint to be adjudicated on
The burden of proof in defamation was incompatible with the campaigner's rights to freedom of expression under the Convention
It was incompatible with the campaigner's rights to freedom of expression under the Convention to allow a big company to sue an individual for defamation
The denial of legal aid prevented the campaigner from having a fair trial under the open justice principle of the Convention
The fast-food chain is a private body, not a public authority, so the scenario cannot engage the Convention

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. D is correct. The scale and complexity of the proceedings confronting the applicant coupled with the denial of legal aid would make the proceedings unfair and an infringement of Article 6 of the Convention and its protection of open justice. Lead case: Steel & Morris v United Kingdom - Case Reference [2005] EMLR 314. Statute; rule; constitution: Article 6.

stem: A man and woman are members of a private limited company which trades as a boutique clothes retailer. The woman is responsible for day-to-day management of the business, with the man a "silent partner". The woman is the sole director of the company, which has no secretary appointed. They wish to raise capital by selling shares to members of the public, but do not wish anyone apart from the two of them to be involved in management of the company.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The man must be appointed as an additional director
The man must be appointed as an additional director and company secretary
The man must be appointed as an additional director and the woman as the company secretary
The man must be appointed as an additional director and either the man or woman as the company secretary
The man and woman need take no further action before selling shares publicly

explanation.en: The correct answer is D. In order that the company can sell shares to members of the public, it will have to relist as a public company. In order to do so, the company requires at least two directors and also to have a company secretary appointed. Either the man or woman can be appointed as the company secretary.

stem: A woman transfers part of her freehold land to her friend. She includes in the transfer deed an obligation upon her friend "for the benefit of the retained land not to use the land transferred for any noisy, offensive or noxious trade or business". The woman subsequently transfers the land that she has retained to her husband. The friend transfers her land to a man.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The husband would enforce the covenant against the friend at common law
The husband would enforce the covenant against his wife at common law
The husband would enforce the covenant against the friend in equity
The husband would enforce the covenant against his wife in equity
The husband cannot enforce the covenant against the friend or his wife

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is A. As the original covenanter, the friend remains liable for the performance of the covenant. The husband could enforce the covenant against the friend as the benefit of the covenant has passed to him in accordance with the common law rules. The friend should ensure that she obtains an indemnity covenant from the man by which he agrees to indemnify her should he breach the covenant.

stem: Section 56 Coroners and Justice Act 2009 (the Act) abolishes the common law defence of provocation and replaces it with a new defence of "loss of control" provisions will apply to defendants charged with murder where the acts or omissions resulting in the death of the victim took place on or after 4 October 2010.
ask: With regard to the Coroners and Justice Act 2009, which of the following statements best describes the trial procedure regarding the reference to "loss of control"?

options.en: unsound and consequently not sufficient to put before the jury

The partial defence may still be put before a jury even if there has been a delay between the trigger event and the murder, and the jury must determine if the time delay was sufficiently substantial to render the loss of control defence unsound and consequently not sufficient to be put before it

The partial defence may still be put before a jury unless there has been a delay between the trigger event and the murder, but the judge must determine if the time delay was sufficiently substantial to render the loss of control defence unsound and consequently not sufficient to put before the jury

The partial defence may still be put before a jury if there has been a delay between the trigger event and the murder, because the judge cannot determine if the time delay was sufficiently substantial to render the loss of control defence unsound and consequently not sufficient to put before the jury

The partial defence may still be put before a jury even if there has been a delay between the trigger event and the murder. The judge must determine, however, if the time delay was sufficiently substantial to render the loss of control defence unsound and consequently not sufficient to put before the jury

explanation.en: E is correct. In relation to the reference "loss of control" within section 54(1)(b) Coroners and Justice Act 2009, it does not matter whether or not the loss of control was sudden. The partial defence could still be put before a jury even where there has been a delay between the trigger incident and the murder. However the judge will have to determine whether the time delay was sufficiently substantial to render the defence of loss of control untenable and therefore not sufficient to put before the jury. The logic behind the judge's authority to remove provocation from the jury is that the defence should not be used in certain types of cases, such as where it is politically or morally unacceptable.

stem: A vehicle struck a person who was walking on the pavement. One of the parties asserts that the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur applies.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the applicability of the doctrine of?

options.en: The doctrine of res ipsa loquitur applies if: (1) the accident is one which would not have occurred absent negligence; (2) the defendant must have had no control of the thing which caused the damage; and (3) the cause of the accident is known

The doctrine of res ipsa loquitur applies if: (1) the accident is one which would not have occurred absent negligence; (2) the defendant must have been in control of the thing which caused the damage; and (3) the cause of the accident is unknown

The doctrine of res ipsa loquitur applies if: (1) the claimant establishes that the defendant has acted in some manner that he ought to be held responsible for the consequences; (2) the defendant must have been in control of the thing which caused the damage; and (3) the cause of the accident must have been an integral part of the defendant's actions

The doctrine of res ipsa loquitur applies if: (1) the defendant in fact caused the loss; (2) the defendant must have been in control of the thing which caused the damage; and (3) the defendant knew or has reasonable grounds to believe that they a risk existed

The doctrine of res ipsa loquitur applies if: (1) the defendant in fact caused the loss; (2) the defendant must have been in control of the thing which caused the damage; and (3) the risk is one against which the defendant could have been expected to offer some protection in the circumstances

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. B is correct. The court may be prepared to draw the inference that the defendant was negligent without hearing detailed evidence of what the defendant did or did not do, provided the following conditions are satisfied: (1) the defendant must be shown to have been in control of the thing which caused the injury to the claimant; (2) the accident must be of such a nature that it would not have occurred in the ordinary course of events without negligence; and (3) there must be no explanation for the accident.

stem: A manufacturer of a drug published an advertisement proclaiming their product would boost male sexual performance. In addition, they guaranteed that anybody who bought the drug, used it as directed, and found that their performance did not improve would be paid £100. A man, having bought and used the drug, says his wife left him for a younger man, and now wants £100 from the manufacturers.
ask: Which of the following best explains the legal position of the parties?

options.en: There is no contract because the man should have given the manufacturers notice of his acceptance
There is no contract because the advertisement was universally distributed, and was therefore not an offer made to anybody in particular
There is a contract because the guarantee to pay £100 amounted to a unilateral contract
There is a contract because, once the man accepted the manufacturer's offer, an implied bilateral contract was formed
There is no contract, because an advertisement cannot be taken to be an offer • which could turn into a contract by acceptance since it should be regarded as a promotional gimmick

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is correct. There is a contract because the inclusion of this statement meant that reasonable people would treat the offer to pay £100 as one that was intended seriously, so that it created a binding obligation. Lead case: Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co Ltd [1893].

stem: After the growth of the government accountability and the establishment of a constitutional monarchy, spurred on by the various electoral reform acts of the 19th century, it became established that the bulk of prerogative powers could be exercised only through and on the advice of ministers responsible to Parliament. Although the monarch retained formal power of appointment and removal of ministers, the development of collective ministerial responsibility made it increasingly difficult for the King or Queen to exercise such power freely against the wishes of the Prime Minister and Cabinet.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes a prerogative power which still resides in the jurisdiction of the personal prerogative of the Crown?

options.en: A prerogative power which still resides in the jurisdiction of the personal prerogative of the Crown is that pardoning of convicted offenders or remitting or reducing sentences

A prerogative power which still resides in the jurisdiction of the personal • prerogative of the Crown is that of giving audiences to ministers, at which Her Majesty may be consulted by and, in turn, encourage and warn ministers
A prerogative power which still resides in the jurisdiction of the personal prerogative of the Crown is that of the conferring of honours and decorations
A prerogative power which still resides in the jurisdiction of the personal prerogative of the Crown is that of restraining aliens from entering the UK
A prerogative power which still resides in the jurisdiction of the personal prerogative of the Crown is that of the granting of royal assent

explanation.en: E is correct. One of the main prerogative powers recognised under the common law which still resides in the jurisdiction of the Crown is the granting of royal assent to legislation, e.g., in 1708 Queen Anne was the last sovereign to refuse royal assent to a bill passed by Parliament. Additionally, no monarchs since the sixteenth century have signed Bills themselves and Queen Victoria was the last to give the royal assent in person in 1854.

stem: A qualified accountant, in her professional capacity as a partner of her accountancy firm, acts as the trustee of a charitable trust. In her personal capacity, she is appointed as the trustee of her late father's will trust. At the end of the financial year, she is asked to review and approve the accounts for both trusts.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The statutory duty of care applies and the accountant owes a higher standard of care when reviewing the accounts for the charity
The statutory duty of care does not apply and the accountant owes a higher standard of care when reviewing the accounts for the charity
The statutory duty of care applies and the accountant owes a higher standard of care when reviewing the accounts for the will trust
The statutory duty of care does not apply and the accountant owes a higher standard of care when reviewing the accounts for the will trust
The statutory duty of care does not apply and the accountant owes the same standard of care in both cases

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is A. As the accountant is dealing with an audit of the accounts of both trusts, the statutory duty of care applies in both cases. In both cases, the accountant must exercise such care and skill as is reasonable in the circumstances, having regard in particular to any special knowledge or experience that she has or holds herself out as having. However in the case of the charity (where she is acting in the course of her profession), special regard will also be had to any special knowledge or experience that she would reasonably be expected to have when acting in the course of that profession. Therefore when dealing with the charity, it is conceivable that she could breach the course or tnat protession. Note that the statutory duty of care applies in all five options. However the standard of care will be higher (than that expected of a lay person) in both cases due to the accountant's skills, qualifications and experience etc. However the standard of care will be elevated even further where the accountant is acting in a professional capacity (i.e. In the case of the charity). stem: The Financial Director of a company produces a report to the board of directors explaining that the company is near insolvency and recommends that the company is placed into voluntary liquidation as there is no way that it can continue to trade as a going concern. The company is the CEO's family business. The CEO is reluctant to accept that it may be wound up. The CEO continues to carry on the company's business as normal with no regard to the interests of its creditors and it eventually goes into liquidation.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: Neither the Financial Director nor the CEO could be ordered by the court to make such contributions to the company's assets as the court thinks fit
The Financial Director but not the CEO could be ordered by the court to make such contributions to the company's assets as the court thinks fit
The CEO but not the Financial Director could be ordered by the court to make such contributions to the company's assets as the court thinks fit
Both the CEO and the Financial Director could be ordered by the court to make such contributions to the company's assets as the court thinks fit
All directors of the company could be ordered by the court to make such contributions to the company's assets as the court thinks fit

explanation.en: The correct answer is E. Where it appears to the court that a director knows or ought to have concluded that there was no reasonable prospect that the company would be able to avoid going into liquidation and that the director continues to trade without taking every step as ought to have been taken to minimise the potential loss to the company's creditors, then the court can order that director to contribute to the company's assets in a liquidation. As the Financial Director has presented a report to the board of directors, then all directors ought to be aware of the company's imminent liquidation. stem: A judge at the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) has, by his personal behaviour, brought the ECtHR in to disrepute. This is a matter of grave concern for his fellow judges. The delinquent judge refuses to step down, however, and the other judges now seek ways to remove him from office. Which option best states the procedure by which an ECtHR judge
ask: Which option best states the procedure by which an ECtHR judge can be dismissed, if at all?

options.en: The other judges must decide by two-thirds majority to dismiss the delinquent judge
The other judges must decide by a simple majority to dismiss the delinquent judge
The other judges must decide by a three-quarters majority to dismiss the delinquent judge
The other judges must decide by a four-fifths majority to dismiss the delinquent judge
An ECtHR judge may not be dismissed, under any circumstances, until his nine- year tenure has elapsed, or when he reaches the age of 70, whichever comes earlier

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. A is the best option. No Judge at the ECtHR may be dismissed from office unless the other judges decide by a majority of two-thirds decide that the judge has ceased to fulfil the required conditions. Rule 7 (Dismissal from office) of the Strasbourg Court states that no judge may be dismissed from his or her office unless the other judges, meeting in plenary session, decide by a majority of two-thirds of the elected judges in office that he or she has ceased to fulfil the required conditions. The judge must first be heard by the plenary Court. Any judge may set in motion the procedure for dismissal from office.

stem: The trustees of a large pension fund wish to delegate their powers of investment to a specialist investment bank who can obtain a better return for the trust's investment.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The trustees are free to delegate these functions to the investment bank
The trustees can delegate these functions to the investment bank subject to complying with statutory requirements
The trustees can delegate these functions to the investment bank only with the consent of the beneficiaries
The trustees can delegate these functions to the investment bank only if authorised to do so by an order of the court
The trustees can delegate these functions to the investment bank only if authorised to do so in writing by the settlor

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is B. Section 15 Trustee Act 2000 provides that where the trustees delegate an "asset management" function, they must also ensure that a policy statement is signed which sets out guidance for the delegates as to how the delegated functions should be discharged. The policy statement must provide for the functions to be exercised in the best interests of the beneficiaries.

stem: A visitor to premises may be a potential customer visiting a shop, a member of a gym, or a patient attending a GP's surgery. Where customers are permitted to be in a supermarket, it may be negligent of the supermarket to leave crushed fruit lying around on the floor for hours, as this presents a possible slip hazard.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes who is a visitor for the purposes of the Occupiers Liability Act 1957 (OLA)?

options.en: A visitor for the purposes of the OLA 1957 is a person who visits the premises
A visitor for the purposes of the OLA 1957 is a person who enters the premises
A visitor for the purposes of the OLA 1957 is a person who is invited or is given permission to be on the premises
A visitor for the purposes of the OLA 1957 is a person who enters or visits the premises
A visitor for the purposes of the OLA 1957 is anybody on, near or in the premises

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is correct. Section 1(2) OLA 1957 defines "visitors" as persons to whom the occupier gives, or is to be treated as giving, an invitation or permission to enter or use the premises. Statute; rule; constitution: Occupiers Liability Act 1957, s.1(2).

stem: A man owns a large property and leaves it to his son in his will. The value of the property immediately before the man's death is £800,000. However, the man had a mortgage of £500,000 on the property which is still outstanding. His son argues that the value of the property immediately before the man's death should not be the value taken, but should instead be the value of the property immediately before the man's death minus the mortgage value.
ask: Which of the following best describes the legal position?

options.en: The value of the property immediately before death is taken regardless of any outstanding mortgages
The value of an outstanding mortgage is deducted from the value of the property immediately before the death of the deceased
A certain percentage of the outstanding mortgage value is deducted from the value of the property immediately before the death of the deceased
A maximum of £100,000 can be deducted from the value of the property if there is an outstanding mortgage
A maximum of £250,000 can be deducted from the value of the property if there is an outstanding mortgage

explanation.topic: Wills and the Administration of Estates
explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is B. An outstanding mortgage is deducted from the value of the property immediately before the death of the deceased.

stem: A wealthy family was the beneficiary of a multi-million pound trust that included a requirement that they 'do their utmost to maintain the integrity of the family estate'. The family would like to vary the terms of the trust, but are thwarted by the trustees. The family has now decided to challenge the trustees in court.
ask: Which of the following statements best identifies the relevant court the family should?

options.en: The relevant court the family should turn to is the High Court (Family Division)
The relevant court the family should turn to is the High Court (Queen's Bench Division)
The relevant court the family should turn to is the High Court (Chancery Division)
The relevant court the family should turn to is the High Court (Administrative Court)
The relevant court the family should turn to is the High Court (Commercial Court)

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is correct. The relevant court the family should turn to is the High Court (Chancery Division).

stem: Your client has instructed you to sell some shares registered in his name using an authorised third person (ATP). You keep a normal attendance note on the client file of your client's instructions. When you actually instruct the ATP to sell the shares you record their name.
ask: Which of the following best represents your recording?

options.en: You have fulfilled all the recording requirements by keeping a normal • attendance note on the client file of your client's instructions and recording the name of the ATP
You are required to keep a copy of the authorisation certificate of the ATP • alongside the normal attendance note on the client file of your client's instructions

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is the best answer. You should also record the details of the ATP. A is not correct. You should keep a record of the times of the instruction and the time that they were carried out, in order to prove that they were carried out promptly. B is incorrect. There is no requirement to keep a copy of the ATP's certificate, although you should ensure authorised to conduct this type of transaction. D is not the best answer. stem: A man is the proprietor of a business that produces one type of shoe in red, green and blue. He keeps all of his stock in three warehouses, one each for red, green and blue shoes. When a client places an order, he takes shoes from the relevant warehouse and delivers them to the client. A woman has ordered 100 pairs of green shoes from the man. Before he is able to dispatch the order, he is adjudged bankrupt and his trustee in bankruptcy seizes all of his stock as forming part of his bankruptcy estate. The woman has already paid for the green shoes and argues that they are held on trust for her.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The woman's green shoes are part of a homogenous mass and therefore form part of the man's bankruptcy estate and are not held on trust for the woman
The woman's green shoes are separated into colours and therefore are not a • homogenous mass. They therefore do not form part of the man's bankruptcy estate and are held on trust for the woman

explanation.en: The best answer is E. When dealing with tangible property, it will be considered a "homogenous mass" and therefore indistinguishable from the settlor's own property unless it is physically segregated. Although all of the man's shoes are separated into colours, some of the green shoes in the warehouse will belong to the man and some will belong to the woman. Unless the shoes comprising the woman's order are physically separated from those forming the man's stock, it would be impossible to identify the specific shoes that belong to the woman. The trust that the woman claimed to have established by paying for the order would therefore fail for lack of certainty of subject matter.

stem: A woman was riding a quad bike through a park. She saw some school friends walking along a path. She swerved the bike towards them, intending only to scare them, but lost control of the bike and collided with them, causing them injury.

stem: A woman is the freehold owner of 123 The Street. In 2007 she grants a lease of the upstairs floor to a man to be used as a dental surgery. The lease contains a covenant by the woman that she will not use the remainder of the freehold as a dental surgery. In 2010, the woman transfers the freehold to her friend and it soon becomes apparent to the man that the friend wishes to sublet the ground floor to a local dentist who wishes to open a practice there.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The man can enforce the covenant against the woman by virtue of the doctrine of privity of contract and the friend by virtue of the doctrine of privity of estate
The man can only enforce the covenant against the woman by virtue of the doctrine of privity of contract
The man can only enforce the covenant against the woman by virtue of the doctrine of privity of estate
The man can only enforce the covenant against the friend by virtue of the doctrine of privity of contract
The man can only enforce the covenant against the friend by virtue of the doctrine of privity of estate

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is A. The lease was granted after 1996 and therefore the Landlord and Tenant (Covenants) Act 1995 would apply. However, following the transfer of the reversion, a landlord can still be held liable for his successors' breaches of covenant unless he obtains a release from those covenants under section 8 of the 1995 Act. Therefore the woman (as original landlord) and the friend (as the woman's assignee) would both be liable under the covenant.

stem: You are called to the police station to advise a client prior to police interview. Your client has been arrested for assaulting a police officer. Your client explains that he likes to take drugs and had been taking drugs before he assaulted the officer. Which of the following best states your client's defence, if any, to any criminal liability arising from his actions?
ask: Which of the following best states your client's defence, if any, to any criminal liability arising from his actions?

options.en: Your client would probably have a defence to a charge of assault under these • circumstances, because he was sufficiently intoxicated to negate the mens rea for the offence
Your client would probably have a defence to a charge of assault based on non- insane automatism under these circumstances

explanation.en: E is correct. Voluntary intoxication under these circumstances may potentially be viewed as an aggravation, but cannot be used as an excuse. Please note that intoxication is a defence to crimes of specific intent and not to crimes of basic intent. The law does not distinguish between the effects of narcotics voluntarily taken and voluntary drunkenness; see, e.g., Lipman [1970] 1 QB 152. Lead case: DPP v Majewski [1977].

stem: Your client been arrested for riot and wishes to have his case heard in the magistrates court. Advise your client as to whether this

stem: Although an offer, acceptance and consideration can be interpreted from a particular agreement, a question may arise whether the parties actually intended to create a legally binding relationship. stem: An implication was made in a photographic exhibition that a member of the British aristocracy had used illegal drugs. The aristocrat seeks advice as to whether the alleged tort constitutes libel or slander.
ask: Which option best describes the distinction between libel and slander?

options.en: Where the defamatory material is by word of mouth, the action will be for libel. Where the defamatory matter is in writing or in some other permanent form, the action will be for slander
Where the defamatory material is by design or malice, the action will be for • libel. Where the defamatory matter is by word of mouth, the action will be for slander

Where the defamatory material is in writing or in some other permanent form, the action will be for libel. Where the defamatory matter is by word of mouth, the action will be for slander

stem: A private company limited by shares has a net asset value of £500,000. The company is looking for some new office space and a director, who is also a professional property developer, advises that she owns a land for future development which the company can acquire for its market value of £70,000.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: There is no restriction on a company's ability to acquire land from a director
There is no restriction on the company's ability to acquire the land from the director as the value of the land does not exceed £100,000
There is no restriction on the company's ability to acquire the land from the • director as the value of the land is below the prescribed ratio of the asset value to the company's net asset value

An ordinary resolution of the members would be required to authorise the company's purchase of the land from the director as the value of the land is above the prescribed ratio of the asset value to the company's net asset value

A special resolution of the members would be required to authorise the company's purchase of the land from the director as the value of the land is above the prescribed ratio of the asset value to the company's net asset value

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is D. Where a company acquires or disposes of a substantial non-cash asset, such as land, from or to a director, then the transaction must be authorised by an ordinary resolution of the members where (A) the value of the asset exceeds £100,000, or (B) the value of the asset is greater than 10% of the company's net asset value.

stem: A wheat farmer transfers part of his unregistered land to a woman. The transfer triggers compulsory first registration. As part of the bargain to sell to the woman, she requires that the farmer gives her a covenant not to use his land for any other type of farming other than for farming wheat.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the way in which the woman can ensure that a subsequent purchaser of the man's land is bound by the covenant?

options.en: The woman does not need to register the covenant as it is contained in the title deeds
The woman should register the covenant by entering an agreed notice on the title to the farmer's land
The woman should register a Restriction
The woman should register a Land Charge
The woman should register a unilateral notice

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is D. As the farmer's land would remain unregistered (compulsory first registration would only apply as to the part transferred to the woman) the burden of the covenant must be registered as a Land Charge. The burden of a restrictive covenant is registered as a Class D(ii) Land Charge against the owner of the burdened land.

stem: A woman agrees to buy 123 the Street from a man. The man executes a transfer of the land to the woman, but she fails to have this registered at HM Land Registry, so the transfer does not operate at law.

The man is the sole legal and beneficial owner of the property
The man holds the property on a resulting trust for the woman
The man holds the property on a constructive trust for the woman
The man holds the property on a resulting trust for himself and the woman in equal shares

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is C. Legal title to the property has not passed since the woman has not registered the transfer. However, the woman became the beneficial owner of the property at the time that the man contracted to sell it to her. A resulting trust in the woman's favour would therefore arise over the property until she perfected the transfer of legal title.

stem: A mother who neither spoke not read English signed a guarantee regarding her daughter's future liabilities. ask: Which category of mistake, if any, would the mother be best advised to plead?

options.en: The mother would best be advised to plead non est factum - 'it is not my deed'
The mother would best be advised to plead res extincta - mistake as to the existence of the subject matter of the contract
The mother would best be advised to plead mistake as to the terms of the offer (unilateral mistake)
The mother would best be advised to plead mistake as to the possibility of performing the contract
A person who has notice of all the provisions of a contract which has been • signed, whether they have been read or not, will be bound by it. The mother, therefore, is bound by the contract

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. A is the best option. The mother would best be advised to plead non est factum - 'it is not my deed'. A party that signs a contract in the mistaken belief that he is signing a document of a different nature may be able to plead non est factum (it is not my deed). A successful plea of non est factum may allow the party to avoid the contract. It must be shown, however, that the mistake was made despite all reasonable care being taken (Saunders v Anglia Building Society [1971] AC 1004). Lead Case: Lloyds Bank plc v Waterhouse [1990] Fam Law 23.

stem: BUM UGU A tenant is claiming against his landlord because he wants his landlord to carry out repairs to the premises. The cost of the repairs is £850.

Where the claimant is a tenant claiming against his landlord to carry out repair or other work to the premises and where the cost of such repair does not exceed £1,000, the case will be allocated to the small claims track of the county court.

stem: A man died on 7 August 2008 leaving an estate valued at £425,000 for Inheritance Tax (IHT) purposes to his wife. The nil rate band in August 2008 was £312,000. His wife died on 6 May 2012 leaving an estate worth £750,000 to her children. The nil rate band in May 2012 was £325,000.
ask: Neither the man nor his wife made any lifetime Which of the following correctly states the amount of nil rate band which can be set against the wife's estate?

explanation.topic: Wills and the Administration of Estates
explanation.en: The correct answer is E. £650,000. None of the man's threshold was used when he died, because he left his entire estate to his wife and he hadn't made any lifetime gifts. So, the wife's personal representatives can transfer 100% of the husband's threshold to increase her threshold. They don't transfer £312,000 - the threshold when the man died - but the percentage of the nil rate band he didn't use, i.e. 100%. They then apply this percentage to the threshold at the time the wife died. Therefore, the wife's threshold increases to £650,000, twice the 2012-2013 threshold of £325,000, using 100% of her nil rate band and 100% of the man's.

stem: A seller failed to deliver goods. The buyer was able to purchase elsewhere at no extra cost. The buyer is considering bringing a claim against the seller for breach of contract.

stem: During a defendant's trial for attempting to defraud HM Revenue and Customs, the prosecution asserted that the defendant fully intended to defraud HM Revenue and Customs but for reasons beyond his control, he failed to complete the offence. stem: The High Court in London has ruled against a hospital's bid to turn off the ventilator that keeps a child alive. The 19-month-old baby has the genetic condition spinal muscular atrophy, which leads to almost total paralysis. Despite claims from medics that the invasive ventilation would cause an 'intolerable life', the parents of the child oppose the hospital's action.
ask: Which of the following is the best advice you would give the parents as to any plea under the European Convention on Human Rights (the Convention)?

options.en: The parents should plead that the hospital will breach the child's right to protection from discrimination
The parents should plead that the hospital will breach the child's right to life
The parents should plead that the hospital will breach the child's right to a private and family life
The parents should plead that the hospital will breach the child's right not to be tortured or treated in an inhuman or degrading way
The parents should plead that the hospital will breach the child's right not to be tortured

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. B is correct. The parents should plead that the hospital will breach the child's right to life. Article 2 of the Convention mandates that contracting States enact and effect criminal legislation that outlaws murder, welfare legislation that allows preventive measures against suicide, procedural, evidential and criminal legislation that allows for an effective investigation into any "taking of life". In NHS Trust v MB & Anor [2006] the High Court in London ruled against a hospital's bid to turn off the ventilator that kept the child, known as Baby MB, alive. The 19-month-old baby had the genetic condition spinal muscular atrophy, which leads to almost total paralysis. The parents of the child fought MB & Anor [2006]. Statute; rule; constitution: Article 2 ECHR.

stem: A man executes a transfer of 123 The Street in favour of his two daughters. He states in the instrument that the land is to be transferred to them "equally" and does not make an express declaration of trust. The four unities are present in respect of the daughters' ownership.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The daughters hold the property on trust for themselves as joint tenants
The daughters hold the property on trust for themselves as joint tenants in equal shares
The daughters hold the property on trust for themselves as tenants in common
The daughters hold the property on trust for themselves as tenants in common in equal shares
The daughters hold the property on trust for themselves as tenants in common in unequal shares

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is D. In the context of the transfer, "equally" would be construed as a word of severance which implies that the daughters are to have equal but distinct shares in the property rather than owning it jointly. Although the four unities are present, inclusion of the words of severance would operate to give rise to a tenancy in common. In the absence of any other presumption or express provision, this would be presumed to be in equal shares.

stem: If the government wants a bill to pass, it is in their interest to ensure that all the areas that need to be analysed have been. For a bill that is deemed by the government to be important, many groups are consulted: experts, Treasury officials if there are major monetary implications, trade union leaders especially, if there are employment issues at stake, MP's, trade organisations etc...
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the role of hybrid bills in?

options.en: Hybrid bills affect the general public but also have a significant impact for specific individuals or groups
Hybrid bills are introduced to ensure that government bills can get through the Lords when the government of the day has no majority in the Lords
Hybrid bills change the law as it applies to the general population and are the most common type of bill introduced in Parliament
Hybrid bills are rules introduced under powers contained in an Act of Parliament
Hybrid bills are introduced only to change the law as it applies to specific individuals or organisations, rather than the general public

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. A is correct. Hybrid bills mix the characteristics of public and private bills. The changes to the law proposed by a hybrid bill would affect the general public but would also have a significant impact for specific individuals or groups. The changes to the law proposed by a hybrid bill would affect the general public but would also have a significant impact for specific individuals or groups. Hybrid bills often propose works of national importance but in a specific area of the UK. Examples would be the Channel Tunnel Bills passed in the 1970s and 1980s that affected the South East of the UK, and - before it was passed - the Crossrail Act to build a new east to west rail link through central London. stem: A man was burnt to death in a car accident caused by the negligence of his friend. The man's father subsequently saw the accident on a later edition of the television evening news, and consequently suffered nervous shock.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes whether or not the victim's father has a realistic cause of action in negligence against the friend?

options.en: The victim's father has a cause of action in negligence against the friend, • because there are sufficient ties of love and affection and he saw the incident on an edition of the television evening news
The victim's father has no cause of action in negligence against the friend, because there are insufficient ties of love and affection
The victim's father has no cause of action in negligence against the friend, because he only witnessed the incident on television
The victim's father has a cause of action in negligence against the friend, because he virtually saw the immediate aftermath of the incident

The victim's father has no cause of action in negligence against the friend, because although there may be sufficient ties of love and affection, he merely saw the incident on a later edition of the evening news

explanation.en: E is correct. Following Lord Ackner's obiter statement in Alcock [1991], the Criminal Injuries Compensation Authority subsequently announced that it would pay compensation up to £20,000 to those relatives that could show "close ties of love and affection" of those killed in the terrorist attack on the World Trade Centre, who suffered psychiatric injury through watching the events of 11th September on live television, but those who merely saw news footage later would not be eligible. Lead case: Alcock v Chief Constable of South Yorkshire [1991].

stem: The incumbent Cabinet Secretary decided to retire after the general election. The new Prime Minister must appoint a new Cabinet Secretary as part of his campaign for greater efficiency in Whitehall. The Prime Minister seeks guidance regarding the Cabinet Secretary's official role.
ask: Which option best describes the role of the Cabinet Secretary?

options.en: The Cabinet Secretary is the Minister responsible for government policy in the Cabinet Office
The Cabinet Secretary is the Parliamentary Secretary to the Treasury and holds • accounts at the Bank of England on behalf of Government departments and selected other public bodies
