stem: A woman and man have recently split up. The woman hears of the man's plans to have a party with his new girlfriend and decides to stop the party from taking place. Despite being asked to leave, she refuses to do so and attempts to stop the party. The man wants her arrested.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the legal?

options.en: Under no circumstances can a person be arrested for trespass
The only option available to the man is civil action
The woman can be arrested for aggravated trespass
The woman can be arrested for trespass
The woman can be arrested for aggravated trespass only if she is violent whilst on the premises

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is C. Under the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 the offence of aggravated trespass is committed when a person trespasses on land when a lawful activity is taking place on that land, or land nearby, and he or she does anything intending to intimidate, obstruct or disrupt that activity.

stem: Your client was walking through a shopping centre when she was struck on the head by falling masonry. As well as causing a hairline fracture of the skull, it has affected her long-term memory and she has not been able to return to her post as a teacher. You estimate that her claim against the shopping centre will amount to £35,000.
ask: Which of the following statements best advises your client?

options.en: Where the claimant does not reasonably expect to recover more than £50,000, the action must be commenced in the County Court
Where the claimant does not reasonably expect to recover more than £50,000, the action must be commenced in the High Court
Where the claimant does not reasonably expect to recover more than £50,000, the action may be commenced in the County Court
Where the claimant does not reasonably expect to recover more than £50,000, the action must be commenced in either the County Court or the High Court
Where the claimant does not reasonably expect to recover more than £50,000, the action may be commenced in either the County Court or the High Court

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. A is the best answer. Where the value of a personal injury claim for damages is less than £50,000, the case must be commenced in the county court.

stem: There is a vigorous on-going debate concerning the development of the law regarding privacy and freedom of expression in light of the introduction of the Human Rights Act 1998 (HRA). This debate concerns whether the courts have interpreted the HRA as Parliament intended. The heart of the tension exists between how courts balance the European Convention on Human Right's enshrining of the right to privacy and with the right to freedom of expression.
ask: How must domestic courts interpret the HRA in the context of interim remedies?

options.en: The court must not have particular regard to the importance of freedom of expression
The court must have particular regard to the importance of freedom of expression, which means that the right to freedom of expression should be given precedence
Although the court must have particular regard to the importance of freedom of expression, this does not mean that the right should be given precedence
Courts must generally shift the balance more towards securing the privacy of the individual
Courts must generally shift the balance more towards securing the individual's freedom of expression

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is correct. Section 12 of the Human Rights Act provides that the courts must have "particular regard" to the right to freedom of expression and cannot grant interim remedies unless satisfied that the applicant is "likely to establish that publication should not be allowed". While Section 12(4) of the HRA requires courts to balance the Article 8 right to privacy with Article 10's freedom of expression; neither is to prevail. Lead case: Douglas v. Hello! (No1) [2001] QB 967, CA. Statute; rule; constitution: Section 12(4) HRA 1998.

stem: A woman executes a trust deed, creating a charitable trust with the aim of providing support and educational opportunities to low income families residing in Oldcastle and the surrounding areas who wish to attend university to study medicine. A girl is from a low income family in Oldcastle and wishes to attend university to study medicine. Her application for funding from the charity is refused by the trustees, incorrectly.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The woman as settlor is able to enforce the terms of the trust against the trustees
The girl as beneficiary is able to enforce the terms of the trust against the trustees
The Charity Commission is able to enforce the terms of the trust against the trustees
The Attorney General would enforce the terms of the trust against the trustees at the direction of the woman
The Attorney General would enforce the terms of the trust against the trustees as the direction of the girl

explanation.en: The correct answer is E. The Attorney General - on the instance of a disappointed beneficiary - is the only person with the ability to enforce the terms of a charitable purpose trust against the trustees. The settlor is unable to do this once the trust has been created and, being a purpose trust, there are no beneficiaries who can enforce the trust.

stem: A patient voluntarily underwent a medical procedure. The treatment caused him to suffer convulsions and as a result he sustained serious injuries. The patient is seeking advice regarding the standard of skill required of the doctor who treated him.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the standard of care used for skilled or professional persons?

options.en: The test for skilled or professional persons is the standard of the extraordinarily skilled person exercising and professing to have that special skill
The test for skilled or professional persons is the standard of the reasonably skilled person professing to have that special skill
The test for skilled or professional persons is the standard of the ordinary skilled person exercising that special skill
The test for skilled or professional persons is the standard of the majority of skilled persons exercising and professing to have that special skill
The test for skilled or professional persons is the standard of the ordinary skilled person exercising and professing to have that special skill

explanation.en: E is correct."... The test as to whether there has been negligence or not is not the test of the man on the top of the Clapham omnibus, because he has not got this special skill.. The test is the standard of the ordinary skilled man exercising and professing to have that " special skill... Lead case: Bolam v Friern Hospital Management Committee [1957].

stem: WILTU - immediate reeaback Parliament is the highest legislative authority in the United Kingdom. Along with the House of Commons and the House of Lords, there is an established monarch (currently Queen Elizabeth II), who remains politically impartial and with limited In light of this statement, which phrase
ask: In light of this statement, which phrase is commonly used to describe the British legislature?

options.en: The phrase 'Queen in Parliament' is commonly used to describe the British legislature
The phrase 'Prerogative in Parliament' is commonly used to describe the British legislature
The phrase 'Commonwealth in Parliament' is commonly used to describe the British legislature
The phrase 'Constitution in Parliament' is commonly used to describe the British legislature
The phrase 'Government in Parliament' is commonly used to describe the British legislature

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. A is correct. The phrase 'Queen in Parliament' is commonly used to describe the British legislature. Please note the 'Crown in Parliament' is used interchangeably with the phrase 'Queen in Parliament'.

stem: On Monday, a man wrote to a woman asking whether she would be interested in purchasing his car. On Tuesday, the woman wrote in reply, 'I am willing to pay £500 for your car and will collect it from outside your house next Monday, if I receive an acceptance of this offer by this Friday.' As the man wasn't going to be at home for the rest of the week, he gave his acceptance letter to his wife and told her to post it on Thursday morning, but he was informed by the woman on Wednesday afternoon that she had already bought another car.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the most appropriate advice to give?

options.en: There is no valid contract, because a valid acceptance requires that it must have been communicated to and received by the offeror
There is a valid contract, because an acceptance is valid from the time that the letter of acceptance has been written
There is no valid contract, because no acceptance is effective until it is received and understood by the person to whom it is addressed
There is no valid contract, because there has been no effective acceptance of the offer, because the acceptance wasn't communicated
There is a valid contract, because the woman was under a duty to wait until Friday so communication of acceptance was not necessary

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. D is correct. If the offeree decides to accept an offer and writes a letter of acceptance which he then forgets to post, there will be no effective acceptance of the offer. The offeror must actually hear the words of acceptance to conclude the contract. Lead case: Adams v Lindsell (1818) 1 B & Ald 681; 106 ER 250.

stem: The Human Rights Act 1998 (HRA) was intended to make the exercise of public power more accountable against basic human rights standards by transposing the European Convention on Human Rights (the Convention) in to domestic law. It was also intended to provide effective remedies in UK courts for violations of human rights by public authorities.
ask: Which one of the following statements best describes the extent to which public authorities are held to account under the HRA?

options.en: If a public authority interferes with a Convention right, complainants may employ the HRA against it by relying on judicial review on grounds of illegality
A public authority may act in a way that is incompatible with a Convention right under the HRA
If a private body infringes a Convention right, it is not possible for victims to use the HRA against it in judicial review proceedings for breach of statutory duty
A Member State may evade its responsibility to safeguard Convention rights by elegating its duty to private bodies or individuals
The definition of public authority in the HRA only includes those bodies whose functions are of a manifestly public nature

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. A is correct. If a public authority interferes with a Convention right, complainants may employ the HRA against it by relying on judicial review on grounds of illegality. The implementation of the Human Rights Act 1998 (HRA) has had an effect on the number of applications for judicial review. While a free-standing application can be made under the HRA, a breach of its provisions may also form the basis for a judicial review application. Since the coming into force of the HRA 1998, a public body's illegality may be challenged as unlawful under section 6 if they are contrary to the Convention, as long as the public authority in question falls within the definition in the HRA (sections 6(3)-(5), HRA).

stem: A private limited company has issued 100 ordinary shares of £1 to each of its three shareholders ("the Members"), who each paid £75 to the company when the shares were issued to them.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: Creditors of the company would be able to claim against the Members directly for any debts that the company could not meet itself up to the value of £25 each
Creditors of the company would be able to claim against the Members directly • for any debts that the company could not meet itself up to the value of £75 each
The company would be able to claim against the Members for any debts that the company could not meet itself up to the value of £25 each
The company would be able to claim against the Members for any debts that the company could not meet itself up to the value of £75 each
The company would be able to claim against the Members for any debts that the company could not meet itself

explanation.en: * of its three lann You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is C. The company would be able to claim against the Members for any debts that the company could not meet itself up to the value of £25 each. As the company has a separate legal personality, its creditors have no ability to claim against the Members in respect of the debts of the company. The Members are only liable to contribute in respect of any proportion of the value of any of their shares which remains unpaid, and this liability is to the company and not its creditors. As the Members in this case have only paid £75 each for shares worth £100, they are liable to the company to pay the remainder.

stem: A woman is the freehold owner of a commercial office block. In 1995 she grants a ten year lease of the second floor to a man. The lease contains a number of provisions, including one that stipulates that the man will not bring any heavy plant or equipment onto the premises that would cause structural damage to the building. The man forgets about the covenant, and halfway into the term installs a heavy safe in the middle of the floor for use by the office staff. One year later, the man assigns his lease to his friend.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The woman can enforce the covenant against the man under the doctrine of privity of contract and against the friend under the doctrine of privity of estate
The woman can only enforce the covenant against the man under the doctrine of privity of contract
The woman can only enforce the covenant against the man under the doctrine of privity of estate
The woman can only enforce the covenant against the friend under the doctrine of privity of contract
The woman can only enforce the covenant against the friend under the doctrine of privity of estate

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is A. As the lease was granted before 1996, the Landlord and Tenant (Covenants) Act 1995 does not apply. The man therefore retains his liability for the performance of the covenants under the lease by virtue of the doctrine of privity of contract. As the woman and the friend enjoy privity of estate, the friend will also be liable under the lease for those covenants which touch and concern the land. Clearly, a covenant not to maim or injure the fabric of the building would touch and concern the land and therefore the friend would be liable to the woman for the breach of covenant.

stem: A man ran in to the road when he saw his friend and was hit by a car. There had been animosity between the two of them, but there was no evidence that the man had issued any threats or that, as a result of his behaviour, the man could have reasonably believed that he was at risk.
ask: Which of the following best describes what actus reus is required for an assault?

options.en: The actus reus for assault requires the intentional or reckless causing of the victim to apprehend immediate application of unlawful force
The actus reus for assault requires the application of unlawtul force against the physical body of another person
The actus reus for assault requires the causing of the victim to apprehend the immediate application of unlawful force
The actus reus for assault requires the causing of any hurt or injury calculated to interfere with the health or comfort of the victim
The actus reus for assault requires the causing of another to fear, on at least two occasions, that violence will be used against him

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is correct. The actus reus of assault is an act which will cause the victim to apprehend an immediate infliction of violence.

stem: Three people worked in a sandwich bar for payment at the rate of £40 per shift. Two of the employees phoned their boss and explained that their colleague was off sick for the rest of the week and that if they were not each paid 50% more until the colleague in question returned, they would close the sandwich bar and go home. Their boss agreed, but is now refusing to pay them the extra money promised.
ask: Which of the following statements best advises the two colleagues concerned whether they have a legal right to the extra pay which they were promised?

options.en: There is no consideration, because the two colleagues concerned were only • promising to do what they were already obliged to do under their existing contract

There is consideration, because by agreeing to the demands of the two • colleagues in question, there would be an increased risk in this type of situation whereby employees would blackmail employers into promising extra wages
There is consideration, because the work shift had become so onerous that it was unreasonable to require the two colleagues in question to continue under such conditions

There is consideration, because as a result of his promise, the boss of the two • colleagues in question did not have to seek a replacement barperson, avoided disruption, and made sure they continued to work
There is no consideration, because a fellow employee being off sick is just part of the normal hazards of working in a bar

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. A is correct. There was no consideration because the two colleagues in question were contractually bound to keep the sandwich bar open. Lead case: Stilk v Myrick (1809). -. person, avoided

stem: A man is a sole trader and wishes to pay his income tax to HMRC in two separate instalments. His friend tells him he is unable to do so and that the tax must be paid in one lump sum at the end of the tax year.
ask: Advise the man regarding the current legal position.

options.en: Income tax must be paid in twelve monthly instalments
Income tax must be paid in one lump sum
Income tax must be paid quarterly
Income tax from one year can be paid in instalments over the next three consecutive years
Income tax can be paid in two instalments, one during the tax year and one following the tax year

explanation.topic: Wills and the Administration of Estates
explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is E. The first instalment is generally due on 31st January of the tax year in question and the second instalment is due on or before 31st July in the following tax year.

stem: A man had been living in England for eighteen months after emigrating from another state. The age of sexual consent in that state is fourteen years of age. Although he barely spoke any English, he invited his fourteen year old neighbour in to his house for coffee and had sex with her.
ask: Which of the following best states the man's defence, if any, to any criminal liability arising from his actions?

options.en: It is a defence under these circumstances that the defendant is a foreigner, and if in his home country his act would not be an offence
It is a defence under these circumstances that the defendant is a foreigner, since under these circumstances, mistake of law becomes relevant
It is a defence under these circumstances that the defendant is a foreigner, and he has been in the UK for less than two years
It is not a defence under these circumstances that the defendant is a foreigner, even if the offence is not criminal in his own country
It is a defence under these circumstances that the defendant is a foreigner, and if his mistake was honest (i.e. not understanding English)

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. D is correct. Ignorance of or mistake as to the law is irrelevant. The citizen is presumed to know the law of the land. Statute; rule; constitution: Esop (1836) 173 ER 203.

stem: While on the way to watch a football match at local rivals Barnham FC, the bus on which Donfield FC football supporters are travelling is stopped and searched by the police who suspect that some of the supporters on the bus are members of the notorious Donfield 'Ultras'. The police suspect that it is likely that by allowing the bus to proceed, a breach of the peace may occur at the end of match planned to take place the next day. The police, therefore, tell the driver to turn the bus around, and escort it along the motorway back to Donfield.
ask: Which option best states the law regarding common law arrest for breach of the?

options.en: The true principle of domestic law is that the police may and must do whatever they judge to be reasonable to prevent a breach of the peace
A police officer may detain a person against his will without arresting him when the police officer perceives a breach of the peace
A police officer and also any other citizen may detain a person against his will without arresting him when the police officer or citizen perceive a breach of the peace
The true principle of domestic law is, that the police may and must do whatever they reasonably judge to prevent a breach of the peace
No preventative action short of arrest can be taken when the perceived breach of the peace is not sufficiently imminent to justify arrest

explanation.en: E is the best answer. No preventative action short of arrest can be taken when the perceived breach of the peace is not sufficiently imminent to justify arrest. In the case of Rv Chief Constable of Gloucestershire [2006], the House of Lords held that no preventative action short of arrest could be taken when the perceived breach of the peace was not sufficiently imminent to justify arrest. In that case, while on the way to an organised and legitimate demonstration, the bus on which the claimant was travelling was stopped and searched. The Police suspected that some of the individuals on the coach were members of extremist protest movements and that it was likely that allowing the coach to proceed would cause a breach of the - - coach back along the motorway. The claimant applied for judicial review, both in relation to the decision not to allow the protestors to attend the demonstration, as well as the Police action in forcibly sending the bus back to London. The House of Lords held that the Police had acted unlawfully and disproportionately by restricting the claimant's rights, under Articles 10 and 11 of the Convention, purely because they suspected that some of the individuals on the coach would cause disorder when the coach reached its destination - where a large number of Police officers would be in attendance. The г -1 - - that the police suspect that it is likely that by allowing the bus to proceed, a breach of the peace may occur at the end of match planned to take place the following day, which is not sufficiently imminent to justify arrest. stem: You are assisting your client, who is buying a house, to find a suitable endowment mortgage. You introduce her to an authorised third person (ATP) and then make arrangements for your client to acquire the policy recommended by the ATP.
ask: Which of the following best represents your position regarding the financial promotion?

options.en: You can rely on the 'introducers' exemption to the prohibition on financial promotions
You can rely on the exemption for one-off promotions to the prohibition on financial promotions
You can rely on the ATP exemption to the prohibition on financial promotions
You can rely on the professional firms' exemption to the prohibition on financial promotions
The prohibition on financial promotions will not apply in these circumstances in any event

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The best answer is B. In order to take advantage of the exemption for one-off promotions, you must reasonably believe that your client would expect to be contacted by you in relation to, and understands the risks associated with, engaging in the investment activity to which the financial promotion relates. One-off non-real time communications, and solicited real time communications are exempt entirely from section 21 without any further qualification, provided the promotions are made personally to one client, or one group of clients, and do not form part of an organised marketing campaign. - romotion? A is not the best answer because this is not an exemption in respect of financial promotions. C is not correct. The ATP exclusion from regulated activities is the appropriate exclusion - but this does not exist as an exemption in respect of financial promotions. D is not the best answer. The professional firms' exemption in (d) is only available when either the exclusion for reasonably necessary work done in the course of a profession (the 'necessary' exclusion) applies, or the 'incidental' exemption applies.

stem: "...You must take reasonable care to avoid acts or omissions which you can reasonably foresee would be likely to injure your neighbour. Who then, in law, is my neighbour? The answer seems to be persons who are so closely and directly affected by my act that I ought reasonably to have them in contemplation as being so affected when I am directing my mind to the acts or omissions which are called in question...
ask: Which of the following statements best summarises the main elements of the 'neighbour principle'?

options.en: The main elements of the 'neighbour principle' can best be summarised as: (1) reasonable prudence; and (2) remoteness of damage
The main elements of the 'neighbour principle' can best be summarised as: (1) rational foreseeability; and (2) remoteness
The main elements of the 'neighbour principle' can best be summarised as: (1) responsible foreseeability; and (2) negative liability
The main elements of the 'neighbour principle' can best be summarised as: (1) negative liability; and (2) fairness
The main elements of the 'neighbour principle' can best be summarised as: (1) reasonable foreseeability; and (2) proximity

explanation.en: E is correct. The main elements of Lord Atkins' 'neighbour principle' in Donoghue v Stevenson [1932] can best be summarised as: (1) reasonable foreseeability; and (2) proximity. Lead case: Donoghue v Stevenson [1932].

stem: Your client - a cruise ship operator - employs a third party company to act as ticket agent. Per the contract between the parties, money collected by the ticket agent is held on trust for the cruise ship operator. The owner of the ticket agent orders his financial director to use the money for the company's own expenses, such as payment of salaries. The financial director carries out his instructions without knowledge that this money is held for the cruise operator. The ticket agent soon goes bankrupt after your client finds out and subsequently terminates the contract. Your client wants to know its available remedies.
ask: What are the available remedies to your client for this breach of trust?

options.en: Your client has no remedy since the third party company is now bankrupt
Your client may seek to recover from the owner personally as constructive trustee
Your client may seek to recover from the financial director personally as constructive trustee
Your client may seek to recover from either or both the owner personally and the financial director as constructive trustees
Your client may seek to recover from the owner of the company personally only if he is decralted bankrupt

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The best answer is B. Your client may seek to recover from the owner personally as constructive trustee. Per Royal Brunei Airlines v Tan [1995] 2 AC 378, where a third party acts dishonestly (an objective standard) and assists a trustee in a breach of trust, the primary trustee's state of mind is irrelevant, and the third party will be held liable as a constructive trustee against whom the beneficiaries may claim personally.

stem: A woman bought a ticket at the ferry ticket office. Although there was neither a sign at the ticket office, nor a disclaimer on the ticket itself, there was a notice clearly displayed in the cabin, which stated: 'The ferry company will not hold themselves responsible for articles lost or stolen, unless handed to reception for safe custody.' Owing to the negligence of one of the crew, a thief managed to get into the woman's cabin, and stole all her valuables.
ask: Which of the following statements best advises whether the ferry company may rely on the disclaimer under these circumstances?

options.en: The ferry company cannot rely on the disclaimer, because the woman was neither under any obligation to read the notice nor to make herself aware of the condition

The ferry company can rely on the disclaimer, because the exclusion clause was • sufficiently drawn to the woman's attention as to be considered as part of the sale agreement between her and the ferry company
The ferry company cannot rely on the disclaimer, because any conditions contained in the notice came too late, as the contract was already made

The ferry company can rely on the disclaimer, because even if they had not taken reasonable steps to bring the extent of the exclusion clause to the woman's attention, she cannot rely on it, as there was already a signed contract in place

The ferry company may rely on the disclaimer, as even if the notice formed a part of the contract between them and the woman, such notices are so standard and ubiquitous that the ferry company is entitled to assume that the woman had previously read such notices

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is correct. Any conditions, or reference to conditions contained on the notice came too late - the contract was already made. Lead case: Olley v Marlborough Court Hotel [1949] 1 KB 532.

stem: In 2013 your client sold an asset for less than he bought if for - meaning he had made a loss of £5,000 rather than a capital gain. He had no other capital gain throughout 2013 but made a capital gain of £20,000 in 2014. Your client wants to know if he can deduct the loss from 2013 from his gain made in 2014.
ask: Which of the following best describes the current legal position?

options.en: Losses are never deductible from a capital gain
Losses are deductible but only if they are made in the same financial year as the gain
Losses made in a previous year to the gain are still deductible
Losses are only deductible if they come from the same type of asset as the capital gain
Losses are only deductible if they follow the capital gain and do not precede it

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is C. Your client can deduct the loss made in 2013 from the gain made in 2014 and reduce the capital gain.

stem: A man was burnt to death in a car accident caused by the negligence of his friend. A hitchhiker who was in the vehicle with the man when the accident occurred leapt from the burning vehicle just before it exploded. Although she was not physically injured, and she and the man were total strangers, the hitchhiker subsequently suffered nervous shock.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes whether or not the hitchhiker has a realistic cause of action in negligence against the friend?

options.en: The hitchhiker has a cause of action in negligence against the friend due to the fact that she witnessed the immediate aftermath of the event
The hitchhiker has a cause of action in negligence against the friend, since she was a primary victim exposed to physical danger
The hitchhiker has no cause of action in negligence against the friend because she suffered no physical injury
The hitchhiker has no cause of action in negligence against the friend because there were insufficient ties of love and affection between them
The hitchhiker has no cause of action in negligence against the friend because • she suffered no physical injury and there were insufficient ties of love and affection between them

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. B is correct. A person who was (or believed herself to be) at risk of physical injury is also regarded as a primary victim and can claim for her psychiatric injury even if she does not actually suffer physical harm. Lead case: Dulieu v White [1901].

stem: Mens rea is Latin for "guilty mind". In criminal law, it is viewed as one of the necessary elements of a crime. The standard common law test of criminal liability is usually expressed in the Latin phrase "actus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea" "the act does not make a person guilty unless the mind also is guilty"
ask: Which of the following best describes the mens rea required to prove criminal?

options.en: The mens rea requirement of the law relating to criminal damage is that a reasonable person acts intentionally or recklessly, and without lawful excuse
The mens rea requirement of the law relating to criminal damage is that a person acts intentionally or recklessly, and without lawful excuse
The mens rea requirement of the law relating to criminal damage is that a person intentionally destroys or damages property belonging to another
The mens rea requirement of the law relating to criminal damage is that a person acts intentionally or recklessly, and destroys or damages property
The mens rea requirement of the law relating to criminal damage is that a person acts intentionally or recklessly, and destroys or damages property belonging to another

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. B is correct. For the purpose of the mens rea of the act of criminal damage, it need not necessarily be intentional, but it does need to be reckless. There is also the requirement that the offence has occurred without lawful excuse, and again this will draw on the beliefs of the individual defendant. Statute; rule; constitution: S. 1 Criminal Damage Act 1971.

stem: A man and woman wish to practice together as solicitors. The man already practices as a sole practitioner and owns a small office building which is already fitted out to be used for this purpose and has been valued at £250,000. They agree that this office shall be used for their new business, although it remains in the man's name. They form an LLP and the woman deposits £250,000 in the partnership account, some of which is used to upgrade the firm's IT infrastructure and the remainder is used for general office expenses.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the?

options.en: Should the LLP be liquidated, the office building would form part of its assets, because the man's liability is limited
Should the LLP be liquidated, the office building would not form part of its assets, because it has not been purchased with money belonging to the partnership
Should the partnership be liquidated, the office building will form part of its assets, because it represents a capital investment that the man has made in the business
Should the LLP be liquidated, the office building would not form part of its assets, because it is part of the partnership's stock in trade
Should the LLP be liquidated, the office building would form part of its assets, because it has been purchased with money belonging to the partnership

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is C. It is clear that the man and woman have each intended to contribute £250,000 to the partnership's capital assets, with the man investing in the building and fittings and the woman investing a cash sum. The building would therefore be regarded as partnership property, even though it is in the man's sole name and it would be available to creditors.

stem: A woman is the freehold owner of 123 The Street, She has received a notice in the post from her local authority advising that they are going to force her to sell 123 The Street to her. She approached you for advice.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The woman owns the land absolutely and cannot be forced to sell it to the local authority
The woman's ownership of the land is subject to state intervention as her estate can be subject to forfeiture by her landlord
) The woman's ownership of the land is only subject to state intervention if she urchased the land from the local authority
The woman's ownership of the land is only subject to state intervention if she is convicted of a criminal offence
The woman's ownership of the land can always be subject to state intervention due to the nature of her estate in the land

explanation.en: The correct answer is E. Compulsory purchase in England and Wales relies upon the principle that freehold ownership is merely a set of rights and duties in relation to the land, with outright ownership being retained by the Crown. It is on this basis that compulsory purchase, with the state revoking those rights, is possible.

ask: Which of the following assertions best states the practical impact, if any, the Humans Rights Act 1998 (HRA) has had on judicial review proceedings?

options.en: A breach of a right enshrined in the European Convention on Human Rights (the "Convention") is not applicable where a public authority could not have acted any differently as a consequence of an Act of Parliament
A breach of a Convention right is applicable where a public authority could have acted differently as a consequence of an Act of Parliament
A breach of a Convention right is not applicable where a private body could not have acted any differently as a consequence of an Act of Parliament
A breach of a Convention right is applicable where a private body could not have acted any differently as a consequence of a Parliamentary Bill
A breach of a Convention right is applicable where a private body could have acted any differently as a consequence of a Parliamentary Bill

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. A is correct. While the HRA makes it unlawful for a public authority to act incompatibly with Convention rights and allows for a case to be brought in a UK court or tribunal against the authority if it does so, a public authority will not have acted unlawfully under the Act if, as the result of a provision of primary legislation (such as another Act of Parliament), it could not have acted differently. Statute; rule; constitution: S.6 HRA 1998.

stem: Three people are the trustees of a family settlement. One trustee feels that he is unable to continue to discharge his functions properly, as his wife has just given birth and he needs to spend more time at home. He has been unable to find anyone to take over his role as trustee.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the?

options.en: The trustee in question's appointment can only be terminated by order of the court
The trustee in question's appointment can only be terminated with the consent of the settlor, the beneficiaries and the other trustees
The trustee in question's appointment can only be terminated with the consent of the beneficiaries and the other trustees
The trustee in question's appointment can only be terminated with the consent of the other trustees
The trustee in question's appointment can only be terminated with the consent of the settlor and the beneficiaries

explanation.en: • scribes the You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is D. Where it is not proposed that an outgoing trustee be replaced with another person to act in their place, the consent of all remaining trustees is required to their retirement. If the outgoing trustee fails to obtain this consent, they will remain liable for the acts of the other trustees after their retirement.

stem: You are instructed by the wealthy father of a child who ordered 7 pairs of very expensive training shoes from a sports shop, but did not pay for them. The sports shop is seeking to enforce payment and intends to show the court that the training shoes have a utility value because they are items of clothing and are not merely luxury items. The father asserts that the child already has an adequate supply of training shoes.
ask: Which option best defines whether the training shoes in question are adequate or not?

options.en: Contracts for necessary goods are defined as: (1) those to the advantage of the minor; and (2) to his future requirements regarding the sale and delivery
Contracts for necessary goods are defined as: (1) those to the condition in life of the minor; and (2) to his actual requirements at the time of the sale and delivery
Contracts for necessary goods are defined as: (1) those that serve the purpose of enabling the minor to earn a living; and (2) serve his actual requirements at the time of the sale and delivery
Contracts for necessary goods are defined as: (1) those to the advantage of the minor; and (2) which are beneficial to the minor, having regard to all the circumstances
Contracts for necessary goods are defined as: (1) those to the condition in life of the minor; and (2) to serve the purpose of enabling the minor to earn a living

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. B is the best option. In common law, some contracts are enforceable against minors, such as contracts for the 'necessaries of life'. - Section 3(3) of the Sale of Goods Act 1979 (SOGA) verifies the common law's approach to goods by defining contracts for necessary goods as those "...suitable to the condition in life of the minor... and to his actual requirements at the time of the sale and delivery...". The fact pattern in the scenario is loosely based on the case of Nash v Inman [1908]. In that case, an undergraduate ordered 11 expensive waistcoats from a tailor, but did not pay for them. The tailor failed to convince the court that the waistcoats were necessary for the undergraduate's status in life and therefore the minor did not have to pay a reasonable price for them. If the training shoes had utility value (being regular items of clothing) and not mere luxury items (such as an expensive necklace) then they are basically in the category of necessaries. Whether so many pairs of training shoes, which can be extremely costly, are necessaries would be a matter for the court on the evidence - taking into account the type of goods and the minor's circumstances. The answer whether expensive training shoes are considered a necessity depends on the social and economic circumstances of the particular child (what the child is accustomed to) and if the child is already adequately supplied with goods of that ilk. Lead case: Nash v Inman 190812 KB |

stem: A judge delivered a judgment in a case. After outlining the facts which she found had been proven on the evidence, she then applied the law to those facts and arrived at a decision, for which she gave her reasoning.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes which legal doctrine the judge's analysis falls under?

options.en: The statement falls under the legal doctrine of stare decisis
The statement falls under the legal doctrine of the ejusdem generis
The statement falls under the legal doctrine of ratio decidendi
The statement falls under the legal doctrine of obiter dictum
The statement falls under the legal doctrine of obiter dicta

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. C is correct. The ratio decidendi of a case is the principle of law on which a decision is based.

stem: Claimants in a case that engaged rights under the European Convention on Human Rights (the Convention) argued that they suffered from serious distress, worry and mental suffering, and that this entitled them to general damages. None of the claimants' accounts relating to their alleged distress and mental suffering gave any details of either any specific medical condition that followed from their distress, or of any medical or other treatment which they sought or received. ask: Which of the following statements best describes the law relating to damages according to the principles established under the European Court of Human Rights qits.litmos.com/course/6267/module/47360/Scorm?

options.en: In considering an award of damages on Convention grounds, damages play very much a primary role
A finding of a violation of Convention rights is, in itself, justification for a damages award
The focus of the Convention is as much on the award of compensation as well as the protection of human rights
The focus of the Convention should be exclusively on the award of compensation, not the protection of human rights
A high threshold of harm is required for domestic courts to award damages in Convention cases

explanation.en: E is correct. A 'high threshold of harm' is required for domestic courts to award damages under the HRA. Courts are reluctant to award damages except in the clearest cases, since damages play very much a secondary role. Where an infringement of an individual's human rights has occurred, the concern will usually be to bring the infringement to an end; any question of compensation will be of secondary, if any, importance. Lead case: R (on the application of Baiai) v Secretary of State for the Home Department [2006] EWHC 1035 (Admin).

stem: You act for directors of a private limited company who have unlawfully paid a dividend. The company did not have sufficient available profits from which to pay the dividend. They seek your advice as to the potential consequences.
ask: What are the consequences of an unlawful dividend payment, if any?

options.en: The directors are jointly and severally liable for any loss suffered by the company due to the unlawful payment
The shareholders are jointly and severally liable for any loss suffered by the company due to the unlawful payment
Both the directors and the shareholders are jointly and severally liable for any loss suffered by the company due to the unlawful payment

Neither the directors nor the shareholders are jointly and severally liable for any • loss suffered by the company due to the unlawful payment if the directors personally cover the full value of the dividend paid out

Neither the directors nor the shareholders are jointly and severally liable for any loss suffered by the company due to the unlawful payment if the shareholders repay the unlawful dividend if they know or have reasonable grounds to believe it was unlawfully made

explanation.en: The correct answer is E. Neither the directors nor the shareholders are jointly and severally liable for any loss suffered by the company due to the unlawful payment if the shareholders repay the unlawful dividend if they know or have reasonable grounds to believe it was unlawfully made. Section 847 of the Companies Act 2006 states that, where there is an unlawful distribution, a member who knows or has reasonable grounds for believing that the distribution was unlawful, he is liable to repay it (or part of it) or, if other than cash, to pay a sum equal to the value of that distribution (or part) at that time. sunnie yi vunus to believe

stem: A woman owns 123 and 125 The Street, both of which are freehold properties. She sells 123 The Street to a man, validly reserving herself a legal easement over 123 The Street to pass over a shared driveway onto the public highway. The man sells 123 The Street to his sister and the woman sells 125 The Street to her friend.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The woman is the owner of the dominant tenement and the man is the owner of the servient tenement
The man is the owner of the dominant tenement and the woman is the owner of the servient tenement
The woman is the owner of the dominant tenement and the sister is the owner of the servient tenement
The friend is the owner of the dominant tenement and the sister is the owner of the servient tenement
The man is the owner of the dominant tenement and the friend is the owner of the servient tenement

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is D. As the legal easement has been validly granted, the burden and benefit will pass to new purchasers of the dominant and servient tenements. The easement was reserved out of the grant of 123 The Street for the benefit of 125 The Street and therefore the owner of 123, the sister, is the servient owner, with the friend becoming the dominant owner when she acquires 125.

stem: A pet owner placed an advertisement in her local newspaper offering a reward of £100 for information leading to the return of her pet cat. A person, who was unaware of the advertisement, found the cat and returned it to the pet owner.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the type of contract, if any, that has?

options.en: No contract has been formed as there has been no acceptance of the offer
The type of contract that has been formed is a simple contract
The type of contract that has been formed is a bilateral contract
The type of contract that has been formed is a unilateral contract
No contract that has been formed as the woman's offer was merely an invitation to treat

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. A is the best answer. No contract has been formed as there has been no acceptance of the offer. The statement is a unilateral offer (or in other words a conditional promise). The pet owner placed an advertisement offering a reward to the finder of a lost pet. In such a case there is clearly a conditional promise and the advertisement would amount to an offer. The acceptance of the offer happens when the offeree performs the act in question. However the finder was not aware of the pet owner's offer so there is no consideration and thus no contract.

stem: A man is the trustee of a large pension trust. In order to liquidate some of the trust's assets to make an advance to a beneficiary, the trustees decide to sell some of the shares that the trust holds. The man has been told that the shares are likely to increase in value significantly, due to an announcement that the company is going to make. Unbeknown to the other trustees or the beneficiaries, the man buys the shares from the trust. The value of the shares increases significantly after the man has bought them.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The transaction is void
The transaction is voidable at the instance of the beneficiaries and the man must account for any profits that he makes
The transaction is voidable at the instance of the beneficiaries and the man must return the shares
The transaction is only voidable if the trust has suffered a loss
The transaction is only voidable if the trustee has not first obtained the consent of the settlor

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is C. A trustee cannot buy trust property from the trust. Where its value increases after he has taken ownership of it, the trustee will be liable to return the property if the transaction is set aside by the court. However, the transaction is not automatically void, and the beneficiaries must make an application for it to be avoided by the court. In this instance, the transaction will be reversed and the shares will be returned to the trust. This applies whether or not the trust has suffered any loss. The settlor is not able to authorise the purchase of trust property by a trustee. •a unsume ine consent

stem: A woman transfers part of her freehold land to a man. She includes in the transfer deed an obligation upon the man "for the benefit of the retained land not to use the land transferred for any noisy, offensive or noxious trade or business".
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: The woman has imposed a positive covenant upon the man
The woman has imposed a negative covenant upon the man
The woman has reserved a positive easement over the man's land
The woman has reserved a negative easement over the man's land
The woman has no interest in the man's land

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is B. The woman has imposed a covenant upon the land that she has transferred to the man. A covenant is a legal obligation imposed in a deed upon the buyer of land to do something or not to do something.

stem: A man and two women are solicitors who practice together in partnership. They entered into a formal partnership agreement which provides that the partnership can only be dissolved with the unanimous consent of all partners and does not contain an expulsion clause. The man is a kleptomaniac and is convicted of stealing a lipstick from a local department store. He is suspended from practice for three months by the Solicitors Regulation Authority. The other two solicitors have recently found it very difficult to work with the man and wish to use his conviction and suspension as an excuse to expel him from the partnership.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the position?

options.en: There is no way that the man can be expelled from the partnership or the partnership dissolved without his consent
The man can be expelled from the partnership without his consent by a court order but the partnership cannot be dissolved without his consent
The man cannot be expelled from the partnership without his consent but the partnership can be dissolved by court order
The man can be expelled from the partnership and the partnership can be dissolved, both without his consent, by court order
The man can be expelled from the partnership without his consent by a majority resolution of the other partners

explanation.en: You did not select the correct answer. The correct answer is C. The court has a statutory power to dissolve a partnership where a partner is guilty of conduct prejudicial to the business, such as an offence of dishonesty, even where the partnership agreement provides that the partnership can only be dissolved by a unanimous resolution of all partners. However the court has no power to expel a partner.
